layers.process: A backcountry permit is needed for hiking or camping in all Navajo Tribal Park areas, US$15 per person per night per location (about A$21 at RBA, 30 October 2026: A$1 = US$0.7040). Carry it at all times on the Nation. Some areas are closed to hiking.

sources.supports: carry the permit at all times

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Respect tribal beliefs: do not climb the monuments (rock climbing is prohibited on Navajo land) and do not scatter cremated remains (cremation is prohibited on the Navajo Nation).
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: Some places, such as Ear of the Wind in Monument Valley, are reached only on guided tours with Navajo operators. Photography, filming, weddings and painting need a special use permit.

laws.rule: All areas are closed to non-Navajos without a valid pass or permit from Navajo Parks and Recreation or another delegated tribal authority; being there without one is treated as trespassing. Monument Valley: US$10 (about A$14.20 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026) per person per day plus US$15 per vehicle.
